note: Independent re-judgment after 562bc0139d, which changed only the comment quote in TestRFC8955TrafficRateNegativeDecodesAsZero to the byte-exact RFC 8955 Section 7.1 text ("On decoding, negative values MUST be treated as zero (discard all traffic)."); no executable statement changed. Positive: 1000.0 (0x447A0000) under subtype 0x06 decodes to exactly rate-limit:1000. Negative: -1000.0 (0xC47A0000) decodes to exactly rate-limit:0 under 0x06 and rate-limit:0:packets under 0x0c (Section 7.2). Both go through parseExtendedCommunities into attribute.appendExtCommTrafficRate, which clamps rate < 0 or NaN to 0. appendExtCommTrafficRate is the only traffic-rate float decoder in the tree (Float32frombits appears elsewhere only in rsvpte, ospf, mrt and bgp-ls), so the decoded value the test observes is the one every reader of the community gets. A decoder that passed the negative through would render a huge or negative rate and fail the exact string equality.
